title: Autumn ENSO gave no clear amount-adjusted link to January-March precipitation concentration in seven California divisions in 1951-2025
abstract: We tested whether autumn Nino 3.4 was linked to the monthly distribution of January-March precipitation in seven California climate divisions in 1951-2025. Concentration was the sum of squared monthly fractions. Separate regressions adjusted for log seasonal total, its square, and year. The equal division mean Nino slope was -0.01087 per degree C. Its 95% five-year block interval was -0.02464 to 0.00239. Thus, the primary test gave no clear link after amount adjustment. This does not prove no link. The unadjusted interval was negative. A six-month window also gave a negative interval, but it includes months used to define the ocean index. The early-period estimate was negative; the late-period interval included zero. These checks limit a general claim of a stable response. The test describes association, not ocean forcing or forecast skill. Monthly data cannot resolve daily extremes or usable water supply. The package includes exact inputs, source hashes, code, all resample scores, a figure, and an independent numerical audit.

display.caption: Nino 3.4 slopes and marginal 95% block intervals. A: each division with amount and year adjustment. B: equal division mean under every fixed design check. Concentration is dimensionless. Negative slopes mean a more even monthly distribution. These are association estimates, not forecast scores.
